title: Single-Leader Read Served without Lease/Quorum Validation
pattern: A replica database node serving read queries directly from local state or cache simply because it flags itself as "leader," without verifying leader validity through active consensus heartbeats or quorum leases.
why_bad: If a network partition occurs, a leader node can be isolated from the majority of the cluster while a new leader is successfully elected by the remaining quorum [42, 81]. If the partitioned node continues to serve read requests because it is unaware of the election, it will return stale, outdated information, violating linearizability guarantees of consensus [81].
detection: Identify methods in replication coordinate classes that evaluate local boolean flags (e.g., `is_leader`, `self.leader_status`) to serve local data reads, without executing a network quorum check or validating an active lease time window with participants.
fix: Ensure read operations are only served after verifying the leader's lease status through active heartbeats with cluster participants, or force reads to query a quorum of nodes to guarantee linearizability [81, 82, 179].
source: Alex Petrov, *Database Internals*, Chapter 14 (Consensus) / passages [81, 82]; Martin Kleppmann, *Designing Data-Intensive Applications*, Chapter 9 / passages [42, 179].
